channel.title: People Seeds
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "People Seeds" - Inspired by the thought experiment by Judith Jarvis Johnson

item.title: Re: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
It was an interesting twist on the standard pod person idea, using dead bodies instead of the usual live ones. Also, linking it back to SCP through the scientist looking to resurrect someone for a reason was interesting.

The only major flaw was that they were babies. They need to come out as adults (or whatever age the entity was at death) and there needs to be some memory transfer, albeit possibly corrupted due to decay, or they would be obvious, especially to loved ones.

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
JamaisJ, to better help the author here, can you elaborate a bit more?

I like the basic idea

But interesting idea!

What about the idea do you like/find interesting, and why? If other reviewers feel like more edits are needed, what do you think the author should keep for sure?

item.title: Re: People Seeds
item.content:encoded:
This is my first time in awhile doing this so here it goes

+ Show
- hope this helps :)

"A plant that unpredictably grows on unmarked or secluded graves."

What does this plant look like? What does it smell like? What does it feel like? I think that when writing this adding other senses other than sight will add more depth to your work

"land in a new place."

What is this new place? Is it supposed to be a dead body? If so please clarify.

"The plant matures into a baby with the exact genetic makeup of the deceased."

How does the plant do this? Is the baby a plant or an animal? How does the plant reproduce? What happens when a person dies? Does it create another instance of this SCP? or does it just die like a human? Do the clones behave differently than a regular person? Can they spread the spores too? How fast do the clones mature? Are the clones really human or is it just an appearance?

"resurrecting and scattering hundreds of them across the nation."

How does this happen? How does the rogue pull this off? What hoops did the rouge do to pull this off? Why so many bodies?

"Foundation to track down and contain the clones of the people they killed"

What struggles does the foundation go through to find them? What takes them so long? What are the consequences if they don't find them?

"Evidence begins to show that a guilty rogue researcher may have planted the SCP deliberately to resurrect a D-class they were attached to."

Why were they attached to the D class? Are they also "looking" for the clones? Where do they come in throughout the story? How are you going to showcase the search? with exploration logs? What are the consequences of his actions?

Overall I enjoy the idea of someone the SCP but I think some more in this details will help

item.title: Re: People Seeds
item.content:encoded:
I like the basic idea, but they're going to need to grow quickly or you'll have a lot of dead babies all over the place. This is also going to a lot of bodies being cremated as well.

But interesting idea!

item.title: People Seeds
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional

Elevator Pitch: A plant that unpredictably grows on unmarked or secluded graves. The plant then releases seeds that drift through the air and land in a new place. The plant matures into a baby with the exact genetic makeup of the deceased.

Narrative: The plant begins to grow on a site where D-class and other Foundation bodies are disposed of, resurrecting and scattering hundreds of them across the nation. The article then follows the efforts of the Foundation to track down and contain the clones of the people they killed (most of whom have reintegrated into society), robbing them of their second chance. Evidence begins to show that a guilty rogue researcher may have planted the SCP deliberately to resurrect a D-class they were attached to.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A heart-wrenching story of love, loss, reanimation, and what happens when a second chance at life isn't enough.
